experiment: Does Strata control-vector abliteration (cvec) degrade flashnext quality on LCB and tau2?
verdict: cvec abliteration removes refusal behavior at -4pp LCB on coding but zero tau2 cost. If the model's purpose is agentic/tool-use (tau2), the uncensoring is effectively free; if coding accuracy (LCB) is a priority, it costs ~4 points.
operational_notes: A combined cvec-on/off driver run failed: a `nohup &` inside a Python subprocess was reaped before the server bound, so cvec-on served=false; and the LCB extractor returned null (list-handling bug). Rerun separately via direct shell script; extracted correct values from the eval JSON.
cvec-on runs on port 8082 (config /root/strata/strata-iq3_s-cvec.json). flashnext must be stopped during its run (same GPU/arena).
deployed config at end: cvec OFF (default flashnext v0.1.44 + adapt-async), flashnext + minicpm-v both active
